description: Turn 7: coref reduces message 5 (20,000 tokens to 50), which is inside the prefix that turn 6 cached. The client did not change, so the change itself breaks the cache. The last breakpoint before message 5 is the end of system, so the provider reads 15,300 tokens and writes the rest. coref saves 19,950 x $0.30 = +$0.00599 and the break costs 19,010 x ($3.75 - $0.30) = -$0.06558, so coref nets -$0.05960 on this turn. The other four operations are applied again as before.
open: design §11 question 12: how Compute knows the earlier operations are still active

design §5.1 snaps B* to the last client breakpoint at or before the previous body's end, and the client's breakpoints are the current request's own: system and the new last message. Read literally that gives the end of system, not the end of the previous body. The examples, and this case, take the end of the previous body.
